page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-384 is a compute-oriented server configuration built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 384 dedicated virtual processor cores and 720 GB of system memory, providing an allocation of approximately 1.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance is provisioned without local storage devices and does not include integrated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Persistent storage and external networking must be attached separately over network interfaces.

The server architecture prioritizes high parallel compute density through its 384 dedicated vCPUs. The lower memory-to-core ratio of 1.88 GB per vCPU creates an execution environment focused on multi-threaded computation rather than in-memory dataset staging. Because local storage is absent, persistent disk throughput and latency depend directly on network-attached storage performance. The lack of hardware accelerators also precludes its use for GPU-dependent workloads.

From an operational perspective, consolidating 384 dedicated execution threads into a single instance offers high compute density while eliminating the orchestration complexity of multi-node clusters. The instance provides a cost-efficient profile for CPU-bound tasks by minimizing excess memory overhead. Primary suitable workloads include distributed source code compilation, video transcoding pipelines, batch processing jobs, numerical modeling, and parallel computational analytics.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-384 is a high-density compute server provisioned with 384 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 720 GB of RAM. Designed around a compute-focused profile, it allocates approximately 1.88 GB of memory per vCPU core, prioritizing CPU throughput over per-thread memory capacity. The instance includes no local storage drives, no integrated GPUs, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring network-attached storage for persistent disk access. By providing 384 dedicated execution threads in a single instance, it delivers substantial parallel computing density while reducing multi-node clustering overhead. The hardware profile is well suited for CPU-bound batch workloads, parallel software compilation, scientific simulations, and video transcoding jobs that require extensive concurrent execution without large working memory footprints.
